18 February, 1972
A BRIEF STATEMENT CONCERNING THE IMPACT OF THE RANDOLPH URBAN RENEVAL AREA PROJECT ON THE AESTHETIC-ARCHITECTURAL-HISTORIC ENVIRONMENT OF THAT NEIGHBORHOOD.
The Project is located partially within the old borders of the town of Sidney of which tere are no visible remains, and just west of the Oregon Hill neighborhood. Prominent city landmarks border the district: Byrd Park to the west and Riverview, Mount Calvary and Hollywood Cemeteries to the south. The project area was the object of a "windshield survey" in late January by two members of the Virginia Historic Landmarks Commission staff. The area consists of attractive early twentieth century middle-class residences in the west regions and more recent small dwellings to the south. Both of these groupings are in the Conservation area and will be preserved. Within the demolition zone, structures are in a generally dilapidated state and for the most part have little redeeming architectural value. We did find that one area, the 200-400 blocks of Randolph Street and the 400-500 blocks (west side) of Harrison displayed several characteristics that might qualify it for placement within a conservation boundary line.:
1. Materials. Predominantly brick residences in good condition, at least in appearance from the street. This street includes the Randolph School, a fine Italianate structure. The frame RCAP Center at the corner of Idlewood and Randolph Streets is a frame building but its superb Queen Anne atvle makes it a real landmark at this important intersection.
